claims.text: The task an async method hands back stands for work that is already under way and not necessarily finished; when the work ends the task holds either the result or the failure, and Task<TResult> is the form that carries a result of type TResult.
claims.source_hint: csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-return-types.md l.53 (a call not immediately awaited returns a Task<int> that contains a Result property)

claims.text: The async modifier allows await inside the method body and has the compiler wrap the returned value in a Task; on its own it does not create a thread or move the method to a background thread.
claims.source_hint: standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/common-async-bugs.md l.23 ('Adding the async keyword doesn't make the method run on a background thread')

claims.text: An async method runs synchronously on the calling thread until it reaches the first await on an awaitable that is not already complete; if it has no await, or every awaitable is already complete, it finishes on the calling thread.
claims.source_hint: standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/common-async-bugs.md l.23 ('runs synchronously until it reaches the first await on an incomplete awaitable')

claims.text: At an await on an unfinished task the method does not block the current thread: the rest of the method is signed up as a continuation and control returns to the caller of the async method.
claims.source_hint: csharp/asynchronous-programming/task-asynchronous-programming-model.md l.122 and l.132 ('signs up the rest of the method as a continuation and returns control to the caller')

claims.text: The continuation of an async method can run on a different thread from the one that started the method.
claims.source_hint: standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/common-async-bugs.md l.52-60 (continuation is posted back to a context; without one it runs on a thread pool thread)

claims.text: If t has type Task<TResult>, the expression `await t` has type TResult; and if t throws an exception, `await t` rethrows that exception, so ordinary loops and try/catch around an await behave as they do in synchronous code.
claims.source_hint: csharp/language-reference/operators/await.md l.32 (type of await t is TResult; if t throws, await t rethrows)

claims.text: Calling a task-returning method without awaiting it starts the asynchronous operation but does not wait for it: the caller receives the unfinished task and continues immediately.
claims.source_hint: standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/common-async-bugs.md section 'Missing await on a task-returning call' (starts the operation but doesn't wait; CS4014)

claims.text: A foreach over an expression of type Task<List<string>> does not compile, because Task<TResult> offers no enumerator; putting await in front makes the expression a List<string>, which can be walked.
claims.source_hint: csharp/language-reference/statements/iteration-statements.md (foreach requires GetEnumerator); operators/await.md l.32 for the type of await t — build the edit to confirm the message

claims.text: If a method returning Task or Task<TResult> throws an exception, the exception is stored in the returned task and rethrown when that task is awaited, not at the point of the call.
claims.source_hint: csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-return-types.md l.66 ('the exception is stored in the returned task. The exception is rethrown when the task is awaited')

claims.text: Task.Wait() and Task<TResult>.Result block the calling thread until the task completes.
claims.source_hint: standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/common-async-bugs.md l.52 ('synchronously block (call Wait, Result, or GetAwaiter().GetResult())'); Task.Wait API remarks

claims.text: Blocking on a task from a thread carrying a single-threaded SynchronizationContext deadlocks when the continuation is left to resume on that context (the default): it posts back to the context whose only thread is the blocked one. A console app has no such context.
claims.source_hint: standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/common-async-bugs.md section 'Deadlocks from blocking on async code', the four numbered steps; synchronizationcontext-console-apps.md l.23

claims.text: When a task's failure is observed through Wait() or Result, the exception is wrapped in an AggregateException, even when only one exception was thrown; the original exception is reachable through InnerException.
claims.source_hint: csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-scenarios.md l.250 (Wait/Result 'wraps exceptions in AggregateException'), l.229-230; Exception.InnerException API remarks

claims.text: A method that uses await must itself be marked async, and an async method never hands back a plain value: a task type — Task<TResult> here — when it gives a value back, and plain Task when it gives nothing, so the caller can await it either way. Awaiting spreads outwards to every caller.
claims.source_hint: csharp/language-reference/operators/await.md l.28; csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-return-types.md l.9-15 (async return types)

claims.text: In an async method declared to return Task<TResult>, the return statement gives back a TResult and the compiler places it in the task the caller receives.
claims.source_hint: csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-return-types.md, section 'Task<TResult> return type' (the return expression is of type TResult)

claims.text: The local variables of an async method keep their values across every await, so a collection being filled in a loop still holds everything added before the method stopped.
claims.source_hint: csharp/asynchronous-programming/task-asynchronous-programming-model.md, section 'What happens in an async method' (the method resumes where it left off)

claims.text: Marking a method async without any await changes nothing about how its work runs: it completes entirely on the calling thread, and there is no waiting to hand back.
claims.source_hint: standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/common-async-bugs.md l.23 ('If the method contains no await expressions ... the method completes entirely on the calling thread')

claims.text: In the example repository at tag stage-0, samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Data/LoadOrdersAsync.cs declares LoadPaidOrdersAsync as async Task<List<string>>, and Program.cs registers LoadOrdersAsync.RunAsync under the sample name load-orders.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: Samples/Data/LoadOrdersAsync.cs l.12 and l.30; samples/DonHang.Samples/Program.cs l.20

claims.text: Three awaits in that file mark a wait on the database — opening the connection, running the SELECT, reading each row — and three are `await using` declarations, one sharing its line with the ExecuteReaderAsync await; the reader yields one row at a time, columns 0 and 1 being id and status.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: Samples/Data/LoadOrdersAsync.cs l.14-25 (OpenAsync, ExecuteReaderAsync, ReadAsync; three await using lines; SELECT id, status)

claims.text: A failure left in an unobserved task stops nothing — the caller carries on, the process keeps running, and the exception surfaces only on TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException, if anything listens.
claims.source_hint: standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/task-exception-handling.md l.50-54 (TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException; unobserved exceptions no longer crash the process)

claims.text: Deleting await from the foreach line of RunAsync in LoadOrdersAsync.cs at stage-0 makes `dotnet build samples/DonHang.Samples` fail with a message saying foreach cannot operate on a Task<List<string>>; the build needs nothing running.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: Samples/Data/LoadOrdersAsync.cs l.32 — make the edit and run the build to confirm the wording

claims.text: A `using` declaration disposes its variable at the end of the enclosing scope, so no close line appears in the code; `await using` declares a variable whose disposal is awaited, so that awaited work also happens at the end of the scope, not on the declaration line.
claims.source_hint: csharp/language-reference/statements/using.md l.18, l.28 (using declaration disposes at end of scope; await using); standard/garbage-collection/implementing-disposeasync.md l.39
